title: Reproduction
seo_title: Secondary 4 Biology: Reproduction Worksheets (O-Level 6093 with Answers)
standard_text: Distinguish between asexual and sexual reproduction; describe mitosis and meiosis and the roles of haploid and diploid cells; describe the structure of an insect-pollinated and a wind-pollinated flower, pollination, fertilisation and the formation of seed and fruit; describe the male and female reproductive systems, the menstrual cycle, fertilisation, implantation and the role of the placenta; describe how HIV is transmitted and ways of reducing its spread (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Biology 6093 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Biology worksheets on reproduction: mitosis and meiosis, flowers, pollination, fertilisation, human reproductive systems, the menstrual cycle, the placenta and HIV. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Meiosis makes haploid gametes; fertilisation restores diploid.
key_sub: Pollination moves pollen; fertilisation joins gametes.
body_html:
How to think about it

Two kinds of reproduction, two kinds of cell division.

  • Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells (growth, repair, asexual). Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.
  • Flowers: anther makes pollen → pollination to stigma → pollen tube → fertilisation in the ovule → seed; ovary → fruit.
  • Humans: egg released on about day 14; fertilisation in the oviduct; implantation in the uterus; placenta for exchange.
  • HIV spreads through sexual contact, shared needles and from mother to baby.
Example

Body cell 2n = 18. Gamete?

meiosis halves the number

Answer: 9

Example

Feathery stigma outside the flower?

catches pollen from the air

Answer: wind-pollinated

Common mistakes

  • Saying pollination and fertilisation are the same.
  • Saying mitosis makes gametes.
  • Saying the mother's and fetus's blood mix.
  • Saying gametes are diploid.

faq.q: What is the difference between mitosis and meiosis?
faq.a: Mitosis gives two genetically identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis gives four genetically different haploid cells, the gametes.

faq.q: What is the difference between pollination and fertilisation?
faq.a: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma. Fertilisation is the fusion of the male gamete with the female gamete inside the ovule.
It lets oxygen, glucose and amino acids diffuse from the mother's blood to the fetus, and carbon dioxide and urea pass back, without the two bloods mixing.
